result.summary: Tracks in-flight manual P2P connection attempts in `CConnman` using a set of pending destination keys to prevent duplicate connections. When `OpenNetworkConnection()` initiates a manual connection, it registers the target in `m_manual_connection_in_progress` and clears it upon exit using an RAII guard. Concurrent attempts to dial the same numeric address or raw hostname string are rejected while the first attempt is pending.
result.problem: Concurrent manual connection attempts to the same target—such as overlapping `-connect` and `-addnode` startup arguments or concurrent `addnode onetry` invocations—race past existing duplicate checks. Because existing checks only verify connected peers already present in `m_nodes`, multiple connections to the same remote peer can be established before either completes.
evidence: PR description fixes #5299, an open issue titled 'Initial connection management' dating back to 2014.

PR description: '-connect and -addnode can attempt the same manual connection concurrently during startup. The existing duplicate checks cannot see a peer until it has been added to m_nodes, so both attempts can pass and open connections.'
result.card: Tracks in-flight manual P2P connection attempts in CConnman to prevent duplicate connections to the same target. Concurrent manual connection attempts—such as -connect and -addnode specifying the same destination during startup—race past existing duplicate checks because those checks only inspect peers already added to m_nodes. Target addresses and hostnames are now reserved during OpenNetworkConnection() so concurrent attempts are rejected while a dial is pending. This addresses long-standing issue #5299 with a functional test exercising concurrent attempts via a proxy handshake.

risk.why: A flaw in reservation tracking could incorrectly block manual outbound connections or trigger an assert on unexpected connection state.
